# OpenFiat — P2P Stablecoin Exchange

> The default web application for OpenFiat, an open protocol for exchanging stablecoins for local fiat currency peer to peer. Solana programs hold escrow and settle; the OpenFiat network coordinates the marketplace — advertisements, reputation, disputes, messaging and service discovery. There is no exchange operator, and no company ever holds a user's fiat.

Deployed at https://app.openfiat.network

## What this app is not

- **Not a custodian.** Fiat moves directly between counterparties' own bank or mobile-money accounts. There is no platform balance.
- **Not an escrow provider.** A Solana program holds the crypto and releases it on the trade's outcome. Neither OpenFiat nor any node operator can release it early.
- **Not an arbiter.** Disputes are decided by independent arbitrators who stake OPEN, cannot see evidence until they commit, and vote by commit-and-reveal. There is no support queue and no operator with a final say.
- **Not KYC'd.** The protocol defines no document verification at any level (OFS-5000). Identity claims are optional, self-published and cryptographically signed; the highest merchant level publishes a business name and support contacts, and explicitly does not imply regulatory approval.

## Current status

Every screen is navigable with deterministic demo data. There is no backend and no wallet signer — all actions are client-side simulations, and the interface says so on every page. It becomes the live application once wired to an OpenFiat node.

## How a trade works

1. A taker picks an advertisement from the order book and opens the order form in place.
2. The crypto locks in the Solana escrow program before any fiat moves.
3. The fiat leg happens on the counterparty's own payment rail — mobile money, instant bank transfer, a local payment app, or cash.
4. The payer marks it paid and attaches proof. Proof is required, because it is what an arbitrator reads.
5. The receiver confirms the money arrived in their own account and escrow releases.
6. If either side stalls or disagrees, a dispute freezes escrow and staked arbitrators decide it.

## Key pages

- [P2P exchange](https://app.openfiat.network/): the order book, with a three-step walkthrough and what distinguishes this from a centralised exchange.
- [Countries](https://app.openfiat.network/countries): 253 countries and territories, each with its own market page, local currency and local payment rails.
- [How to buy](https://app.openfiat.network/guide/buy): fiat on-ramp, step by step.
- [How to sell](https://app.openfiat.network/guide/sell): fiat off-ramp, including the one rule that matters — never release before checking your own account.
- [How to become a merchant](https://app.openfiat.network/guide/merchant): the OPEN bond, the liquidity vault, and what being a merchant commits you to.
- [Disputes](https://app.openfiat.network/disputes): arbitrator eligibility, and cases at each stage of the lifecycle.
- [Governance](https://app.openfiat.network/governance): OPEN-weighted proposals and treasury.
- [Service providers](https://app.openfiat.network/providers): the permissionless service registry.
- [Register a service](https://app.openfiat.network/providers/register): what a signed registration event requires. No application, no reviewer.
- [Network](https://app.openfiat.network/network): nodes, peers and the protocol event stream.
- [OPEN token](https://app.openfiat.network/open): the presale. OPEN is 1:1 with USDC and has no P2P market until mainnet.

## Assets and currencies

Stablecoins: USDT, USDC, USD1. Plus SOL. OPEN is the protocol's own token — staked by merchants, arbitrators, node operators and service providers as accountability, and used for governance. It is not the asset being traded.

91 fiat currencies have local payment rails; every market also accepts cash, in person or as a bank deposit, because cash is the only rail that exists everywhere.

## Reputation

Eight independent dimensions per OFS-3000, not one score: settlement speed, trade success rate, dispute rate, trade volume, average ticket size, merchant age, availability, payment accuracy. The protocol deliberately defines no formula for combining them. Where this app shows a single figure, it summarises the five that describe conduct and says so — volume, ticket size and account age describe scale, not behaviour.

## Specifications

The protocol is defined in 26 numbered specifications and a 28-chapter whitepaper: https://github.com/OpenFiat-org/openfiat-specs

Ones this app implements against most directly:

- OFS-2100 — Advertisement Protocol
- OFS-2300 — Settlement Protocol
- OFS-2400 — Dispute Protocol
- OFS-3000 — Reputation Engine
- OFS-1500 — Service Registry Protocol
- OFS-5000 — Identity Claims Protocol
